chef.background: Founded by husband-and-wife duo Arya Masagung and Angeline Chandraatmadja, Saikyo Pasta was inspired by Tokyo mom-and-pop kissaten diners. After testing over 7 ketchups, 10 soy sauces, and hundreds of dashi simmerings as a cult home-based business, they brought their comforting, unpretentious Japanese-Italian creations to an intimate 12-seater counter bar at Icon Village, Tanjong Pagar.

intro.headline: From a Passion-Driven Home Kitchen to Tanjong Pagar
paragraphs: Saikyo Pasta was born out of late-night trips to Tokyo, wandering through quiet backstreets and falling in love with unassuming mom-and-pop kissaten diners that served comforting, soul-warming bowls of Japanese-Italian pasta.

Before opening at Icon Village, founders Arya and Angeline spent months obsession-testing every element in their home kitchen: cycling through 7 types of ketchup, 10 artisanal soy sauces, and 3 varieties of eringi mushrooms until the balance of sweet, savory, and umami was unmistakable.

At our intimate 12-seat counter, there are no shortcuts. Every bowl is simmered fresh upon order: our signature mentaiko is crafted dairy-free with pure dashi and ocean freshness, while our Napolitan is caramelized in butter and extra virgin olive oil for that warm, nostalgic hug.

craftFeature.title: Pure Ocean Mentaiko and Homemade Dashi Are Just The Start
bodyParagraphs: Unlike commercial mentaiko pastas laden with heavy cream or milk, our secret mentaiko sauce is built on an ocean-fresh dashi reduction and succulent tiger prawns.
Every bite pops with bright umami, finished with crisp mekabu seaweed and fresh Japanese shiso leaf.

story.title: Late Nights, 10 Soy Sauces, and a Dream of Authentic Wafu Comfort
paragraphs: When Arya Masagung and Angeline Chandraatmadja returned from Tokyo, they could not stop thinking about the comforting plates of pasta they had eaten at humble neighbourhood diners. Rather than accepting heavy, westernized adaptations, they set out to recreate that precise balance at home.

What followed was three months of obsessive kitchen experiments: tasting seven ketchups to find the one with just the right acidity to caramelize gently in butter, simmering ten different artisanal soy sauces, and precision-sautéing eringi mushrooms into scallop-like coins.

Their home-based business gained a passionate following across Singapore, leading to their permanent 12-seat diner at Icon Village. Here, Chef Keisuke and the founding team cook every portion directly in front of diners at the wooden counter.
story.quote: We cycled through 7 ketchups, 10 soy sauces, and 3 months of late nights to bring authentic wafu pasta to Tanjong Pagar.
